steps.text: A pawn is the only piece that attacks different squares than it walks to. It walks straight and attacks at an angle. In a crowded position you must keep those two jobs apart. Watch the three boards, then try one yourself.

steps.caption: The pawn on e2 can capture the bishop on d3, because d3 is a forward diagonal with an enemy piece on it.

line.say: The pawn captures diagonally: it takes the bishop and now stands on d3.
Black replies with the knight. It was never attacked by the pawn on d3, which watches only c4 and e4.

steps.caption: The same pawn can capture the other way too: the knight on f3 stands on the other forward diagonal.

line.say: Capturing on the other side moves the pawn to the f-file for good.
Black makes a waiting move with the king.

steps.caption: Forward works differently. Both e3 and e4 are empty, so the pawn on its starting square may jump two.

line.say: Both squares ahead were empty, so the two-square jump is allowed.
The bishop can capture the pawn that jumped next to it.

steps.text: Before you look for squares, **name the piece** and check its colour. White pawns walk up the board and black pawns walk down. The rules are the same, only the direction flips. A common slip [H]: using White's direction for a black pawn. Check the colour every time.

steps.caption: White walks up, Black walks down. Two pawns on the same file therefore head toward each other.

line.say: White's pawn jumps up from its starting square.
Black's pawn jumps down. The two pawns now face each other.

steps.caption: Black to move. The pawn on d7 can capture the bishop on e6: its forward diagonals point down the board.

line.say: The black pawn captures downward and to the side, taking the bishop.

steps.caption: A black pawn that has already moved goes one square at a time. This one can step to d4 or capture on c4 or e4.

line.say: Black captures the rook. The pawn on e4 now attacks d3 and f3.

steps.text: **Remember.** A pawn walks straight but captures at an angle, so keep those two jobs apart. Check its colour first: White walks up the board, Black walks down. It captures only on a forward diagonal with an enemy piece. From its starting square it may jump two, if both squares are empty.
